articles.title: From international transfers to everyday banking: How cross-border finance is changing
articles.summary: Moving to another country often means starting over in more ways than one.
articles.body: Moving to another country often means starting over in more ways than one. From rebuilding a credit history and finding suitable banking services to managing everyday expenses and supporting family back home, people living across borders face financial challenges that don't always reflect their actual earning potential or financial track record.As international migration continues to grow, so does the need for financial services that can keep pace with increasingly global lives. According to the UN, an estimated 304 million people1 live outside their country of birth, while remittances have become an important source of financial support for families worldwide. Yet, financial systems often remain divided by national boundaries, making it difficult for people to manage their money seamlessly across countries.LemFi, the financial platform for people building lives across borders, announced its new global brand platform, alongside a completely rebuilt app, launching the largest product expansion in its history.More than two million customers rely on LemFi to move money to more than 30 countries, with over $2 billion in monthly transaction volume, and the company plans to add more countries next year. The expanded platform, “Ambition has no passport”, brings savings and credit in the UK, eSIMs in more than 150+ destinations, alongside LemFi’s existing international payments service.People who move countries arrive with a career, a qualification and a savings record, only to find that almost none of it counts. A credit history rarely survives a border crossing. Around 304 million people now live outside the country where they were born, sending some $905 billion home each year. Yet many financial services remain designed around individual products or customers living their financial lives in a single country. LemFi is building its platform around that gap, extending from the international transfers on which the company was founded into a wider range of financial services designed for people whose lives span borders.“We started LemFi because sending money home was broken. What we learned is that the harder problem starts after the transfer,” said Ridwan Olalere, co-founder and CEO of LemFi. “Our customers are building careers and businesses in one country while supporting people in another, and the financial system treats them as if they can only exist in one place at a time. That is the wrong answer for people this ambitious, so we have rebuilt LemFi to work the way their lives do. Ambition travels. The infrastructure behind it should travel too.”Inside LemFi’s expanded platformTransfers, still at the heart of it. Send money to more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe and beyond, from the same account that now saves, borrows and connects.Savings that stay within reach in the UK. The LemFi Instant Access Savings Account currently pays a boosted 5% AER for the first six months from account opening; it then reverts to 3.04% AER (tracker), tracking the Bank of England base rate. Accounts open from £1, with no penalty for withdrawals. Deposits are held by ClearBank and protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) up to £120,000 per eligible depositor.A credit history that travels in the UK. A revolving credit line, available subject to availability, is issued by Lemfi Credit through Pillar, the FCA-regulated credit provider LemFi acquired in 2025. It is available as a virtual card through Apple Pay and Google Pay and can be used for both spending and sending. Eligible customers can also see their Equifax credit score in the app for free.eSIM in more than 150+ destinations, in every market. Buy mobile data before arriving, with no SIM swap and no roaming bill.A brand and an app rebuilt togetherThe app has been re-architected from the ground up to hold several products across several countries in a single account, rather than bolting them onto a transfer app. The redesign also brings LemFi’s products to the forefront of the experience, making them easier to discover and creating an architecture that lets the company add new services as it expands.LemFi has also introduced its new global brand platform, “Ambition has no passport”, reflecting its focus on customers building careers, businesses, families and financial lives across borders. The new identity spans LemFi’s product interface, website, marketing and social channels and will roll out across its global markets.“LemFi started as a way to send money home. Our customers turned it into a way to build a life across borders,” said Isabel Ron-Pedrique, VP of Design and Brand at LemFi. “They are not defined by the country they left. They are defined by what they are building. Ambition has no passport is not a line we placed on top of the product. It is the idea the whole system is built from, from the app you open in the morning to the poster you walk past on the way to work. We have built this brand to keep up with them”Savings and credit are available in the UK at launch, with other markets to follow.Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.Reference/s:1. use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Consumers becoming more discerning; creating opportunities beyond traditional coffee occasions:’ Rajat Agrawal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Coffee lovers in India are becoming more discerning, creating opportunities for cafes to go beyond the regular products.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Coffee lovers in India are becoming more discerning, creating opportunities for cafes to go beyond the regular products. Barista Coffee CEO Rajat Agrawal sees increasing demand for premium coffee, matcha, bubble tea and protein-led beverages reflecting different tastes, lifestyles and consumption needs. Excerpts:Ques. How is coffee consumption in India changing with time?Ans. Consumers are becoming more curious and discerning, and that is creating opportunities beyond traditional coffee occasions. For organised café chains, the opportunity is to innovate while keeping the menu focused, operationally practical and commercially viable. We look at taste, ingredient quality, customer interest, preparation time, sourcing reliability and contribution margins before scaling a new product.Pricing must communicate value rather than simply follow trends. A balanced portfolio with familiar favorites, accessible upgrades and selective premium or functional options can attract new customers, encourage trial and support higher-value visits.Ques. As competition intensifies in India’s café sector, what is becoming the bigger differentiator for brands: product quality, ambience, convenience or the overall customer experience?Ans. Product quality is the foundation, but the differentiator is increasingly the experience customers receive every time they visit. Great coffee must be supported by warm service, a comfortable and relevant space, dependable availability and convenient ways to order.At Barista, we see a café as more than a place to buy a beverage, it is a space for connection, work and everyday moments. We are focused on consistency across product and service, relevant menu innovation, accessible formats and stronger engagement with customers. Loyalty is earned through the small details repeated well, remembering preferences, delivering on expectations and giving people a reason to return.Ques. What are the key factors that determine the profitability of an individual café and how do you evaluate the commercial viability of a new outlet?Ans. A café’s profitability is shaped by a combination of location, rentals, customer footfall, average bill value, product mix, operating costs and the ability to generate repeat visits. Strong sales alone do not guarantee healthy economics, disciplined control over food costs, manpower, wastage, utilities and delivery commissions is equally important.We evaluate a proposed outlet through catchment potential, consumer profile, visibility, accessibility, competitive intensity and realistic revenue projections. We also assess the investment required, expected payback and operational feasibility. The objective is not simply to open more cafés, but to build outlets that can sustain profitable operations over the long term.Ques. Barista just opened its 555 café. What has driven this growth?Ans. Reaching 555 cafés reflects the strength of our brand, the trust of our customers and the commitment of our teams and partners. Our growth has been driven by a clear proposition: making quality coffee and welcoming café experiences accessible across diverse markets. As we expand, we remain focused on choosing the right locations and formats, strengthening training and operating processes, and maintaining consistency in sourcing, preparation and service.We believe expansion and efficiency must move together. Each new café has to fit the local market, meet our operating standards and contribute to a healthy business. Sustainable growth is ultimately about building capability, not just adding outlets.Ques. How do you adapt the business model to local consumer behaviour?Ans. A successful city strategy begins with understanding how people live, work, socialise and consume. We study the local catchment, customer profile, price expectations and food preferences before shaping the outlet proposition. The core experience remains consistent, while the menu, communication and operating choices can respond to local demand.In markets where customers seek a more substantial food occasion, for example, freshly prepared food can complement the coffee offering and increase relevance across breakfast, lunch and evening visits. The aim is to strike the right balance: local relevance without losing the brand’s identity, and customer choice without creating unnecessary operational complexity.You use AI every day. articles.title: Wendy's turned down Nelson Peltz's $1.4 billion offer. It's betting instead on thicker bacon and whole-leaf lettuce.
articles.summary: Change is being cooked up at Wendy's.
articles.body:
Wendy's ( WEN ) new CEO Bob Wright just revealed his plan to save the ailing fast food chain, and it looks a lot like the one Burger King ( QSR ) ran to rack up huge sales in 2026.

The plan hinges on a return to better food quality if fast food diners are going to pay inflationary prices.

"We are also rebuilding our food offerings and have begun testing improvements to quality and craveability of our core items, including thicker, crispier bacon, a richer and creamier Frosty, whole leaf lettuce on sandwiches, and improved salads," Wright said on his earnings call Thursday morning.

Wendy's conviction in its turnaround attempt, called Dave's Way, has led the company to reject a $1.4 billion buyout offer from billionaire investor Nelson Peltz's Trian Partners.

"The Independent Committee thoroughly evaluated this Proposal and unanimously concluded that it substantially undervalues Wendy's standalone prospects and long-term earnings potential," Wendy's board chair Art Winkleblack wrote in a statement . "Our confidence rests firmly in Bob Wright's proven track record of seasoned industry leadership, including restaurant business turnarounds."

The company will have a lot of work to do to turn around the struggling fast food business.

In the third quarter, Wendy's reported US same-store sales declined 5.7%, marking the company's seventh straight quarter of comparable sales declines, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace analysis.

Wendy's reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.13, beating Wall Street's estimates of $0.09. Third quarter revenue of $547 million declined 0.5% year over year but came in ahead of the Street's estimate of $531 million, per S&P Global Market Intelligence.

The restaurant chain has also been dealing with franchisees shuttering locations amid severe margin pressures. In September, Meritage Hospitality Group, one of Wendy's largest franchise operators, with more than 300 locations, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection following an escalating dispute with corporate headquarters.

Wendy's said Thursday it plans to acquire up to 163 Wendy's restaurants from Meritage.

"WEN appears to have aligned the system around Dave's Way, altered its approach to breakfast and has plans for greater portfolio changes, all of which should help the longer-term story," Citi analyst Jon Tower wrote in a note. "However, this will be overshadowed by potential M&A headlines and short of WEN indicating M&A is off the table, we see a floor on share performance today."

articles.title: Stocks outside the AI trade are rallying — and Washington just added fuel
articles.summary: Investors are buying travel, housing, and value stocks after the midterms while dumping the chip stocks that led the AI boom.
articles.body:
The election gave Wall Street a reason to buy almost everything. Chip stocks are the exception, and they've lost nearly $4 trillion in value since early October.

Democrats' sweep of both chambers of Congress sent the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) up 3% on Wednesday, its best day since the April 9, 2025, rally that followed President Trump's pause on his "Liberation Day" tariffs. Roughly three out of every four S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) stocks rose in a rally few expected .

Apple ( AAPL ) and Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK-B ) closed at records. Airlines, homebuilders and retailers jumped as oil fell below $90 a barrel on bets that the war in Iran is winding down. Home Depot ( HD ) and Lowe's ( LOW ) had their best days since November 2022.

Chips went the other way. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell 3% Wednesday, deepening the new bear market it entered Monday , and chip stocks slid again in premarket trading Thursday after Qualcomm's outlook fell short .

The election didn't start this rotation. It sped it up.

In October, the S&P 500 fell just 0.9%, but "rotation within the market was dramatic," BofA equity strategist Savita Subramanian wrote in a BofA Global Research report. Some 76% of S&P 500 stocks beat the index, the best breadth in BofA's data back to 1986, and the equal-weight S&P 500 ( ^SP500EW ) beat the regular index by the widest margin since April 2009.

The damage in chips is enormous. Since Nvidia's ( NVDA ) record close on Oct. 6, 29 major chip stocks have lost about $3.8 trillion in market value through Wednesday, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. Nvidia alone has shed about $940 billion. Over the same stretch, the other 474 stocks in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 gained about $1.5 trillion.

Washington is adding to the pressure. Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have pushed a moratorium on new AI data centers , and their party now controls both chambers. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF ( SMH ) has also fallen below the $520 level BofA's Michael Hartnett flagged as one chip bulls needed to hold .

"How do you stay in the AI trade through all the whipsaws and the roller coaster and not get seasick? You have to actually own a barbell," Drew Pettit, chief investment strategist at Roundhill Investments, said on Yahoo Finance on Wednesday.

Value stocks are finally having their moment

The clearest read on the rotation is value versus growth . The iShares Russell 1000 Value ETF ( IWD ) is up about 26% this year, while the iShares Russell 1000 Growth ETF ( IWF ) is roughly flat. Since early October, value has gained about 6% while growth has dropped about 8%.

articles.title: Record share of first-time homebuyers paying in cash as Great Wealth Transfer picks up steam
articles.summary: 10% of first-time homebuyers paid all in cash, a sign that inheritances or other family gifts helped them get there.
articles.body:
The Great Wealth Transfer is starting to impact the housing market.

A record share of first-time homebuyers are paying for their properties in cash, a sign that more buyers are likely using money they inherited from older generations to help fund their purchases.

Last year, 1 in 10 first-time buyers did an all-cash transaction, according to a new report from the National Association of Realtors, the fourth straight year with an increase, and the largest share since the trade group began collecting data on those transactions in 2003. Among first-time all-cash buyers, 28% reported using an inheritance to help fund their deal, compared with just 9% of first-time buyers who financed.

As home prices hover near all-time highs and mortgage rates stay north of 7% , pricing out many prospective buyers, some portion of those buyers may simply be waiting for an inheritance or other significant help from wealthy baby boomers or members of the Silent Generation.

"It is critical when analyzing first-time buyers to understand there is a growing divide among those who are saving independently and priced out of homeownership, versus those who are waiting on the sidelines but then given a generational transfer of wealth," the report said.

Buyers reliant on wealth transfers look different from those who finance and use their own savings. As modern life expectancy increases, delaying inheritances, first-time all-cash buyers are typically deep into middle age. The median first-time buyer paying all cash is 54 years old, according to the report, significantly older than the median age of 38 for first-time buyers financing their homes.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Novavax boosts 2026 revenue forecast as licensing deals pay off
articles.summary: Nov 5 (Reuters) - Vaccine maker Novavax raised its annual revenue forecast above Wall Street expectations on Thursday, banking on payments ‌related to its li...
articles.body:
Nov 5 (Reuters) - Vaccine maker Novavax ( NVAX ) raised its annual revenue forecast above Wall Street expectations on Thursday, banking on payments ‌related to its licensing deals.

Shares of the company fell 9% ‌to about $9 during Thursday trading.

The company has relied on licensing deals and partnerships tied to ​its protein-based vaccine platform and its Matrix-M adjuvant — a compound that boosts the body's immune response to vaccines.

Novavax now expects 2026 adjusted revenue between $385 million and $415 million, higher than $235 million to $275 million previously and analysts' average estimate of $380.29 million, according ‌to data compiled by ⁠LSEG.

The loss-making company is betting on the licensing agreement with French drugmaker Sanofi, worth at least $1.2 billion, to reach profitability ⁠by 2028.

"We intend to bring new partners forward and it is core to our business model. So not only are we open to it, but we proactively ​try to ​facilitate and seek that," Novavax CEO ​John Jacobs said in an interview.

The ‌company is running experiments to assess the impact of adding its Matrix-M adjuvant to existing shots, having evaluated more than 30 commercialized vaccines globally, Jacobs told Reuters.

Sanofi plans a late-stage US trial of its influenza-COVID-19 combination vaccine, which uses Novavax's COVID-19 vaccine Nuvaxovid, in 2027. Novavax is eligible for a ‌milestone payment of $225 million upon US commercial launch.

The ​Democrats' sweep in the US midterm elections ​has lifted hopes of stability ​in vaccine policy after a period of uncertainty.

"I think it's ‌too early to tell in the ​immediacy what may exactly ​happen there ... I do think that could bode well over time for vaccine manufacturers," Jacobs said.

Novavax is also exploring vaccines for bacterial and ​fungal infections, as well ‌as cancer.

It posted a quarterly net loss of $31 million, compared with ​a net loss of $202 million a year ago.

articles.body: Indian equity markets recorded their sharpest single-day rise in seven months on Thursday, supported by a decline in oil prices following the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections. articles.title: Toyota stock surges as hybrid sales, weaker yen boost profit forecast
articles.summary: Toyota (TM) stock is jumping on the back of a guidance raise, as the Japanese auto giant shows its hybrid bet is paying off.
articles.body:
Toyota ( TM ) stock is jumping on the back of a guidance raise, as the Japanese auto giant shows its hybrid bet is paying off.

The world's largest automaker reported fiscal Q2 profit fell 19% from a year ago; however, the company raised its full-year operating income forecast to 3.9 trillion yen ($24.7 billion) from 3.4 trillion ($21.5 billion), citing strong sales in select regions and cost-cutting efforts.

"In addition to reduced tariff-related costs, through the accumulation of improvement efforts, including the expansion of value chain earnings, we expect year-on-year profit growth, and have revised our forecast upward," Toyota Accounting Group Chief Officer Takanori Azuma said in a presentation.

Toyota stock jumped over 9% in New York, its biggest one-day move since July of last year, when the stock rose over 13% on news that the US and Japan reached a trade deal on auto tariffs. Toyota shares listed in Tokyo soared 17%, its biggest one-day move since 1987, per Bloomberg .

Toyota also benefits from a weaker yen, which gave it a forex boost of 685 billion yen ($4.3 billion) in the first half of the fiscal year.

While regions like China suffered, Japan and North America grew or maintained their existing sales levels. In the US, hybrid offerings like the Camry and RAV4 SUV remained popular. Last month, Toyota reported its "electrified" vehicle sales (which include both hybrids and EVs) jumped 28.5% to 363K units, representing 57.4% of total sales volume.

"North America returned to profitability largely due to price revisions and the reduced impact of U.S. tariffs," Azuma said.

The gains are expected to continue, with Toyota forecasting North America market share of HEV (hybrid electric vehicles) rising to 15.6% from 12.7%, whereas pure EV share is expected to drop to 5.8% from 7.8%.

Toyota also expanded its buyback program to up to 1.3 trillion yen ($8.2 billion), targeting 14 trillion yen ($88.7 billion) in shareholder returns over the next 5 years.

Pras Subramanian is the lead auto reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram .

articles.title: Britannia profit rises 11% to Rs 726 cr
articles.summary: Britannia Q2 FY27 net profit rises 10.8% to Rs 726 crore as total income jumps 15.9% to Rs 5,671 crore; raw material costs up 22.3% amid inflation.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Britannia Industries reported a 10.8% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 726 crore for the September quarter, even as expenses grew faster than income. It had posted a profit of Rs 655 crore a year earlier.Total income rose 15.9% to Rs 5,671 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 4,893 crore in the corresponding period last year.The biscuit maker reported 13% growth in sales volumes, which measure the quantity sold. Sales of goods rose 16.6% to Rs 5,542 crore from Rs 4,752 crore a year earlier.“We sustained strong top-line momentum during the quarter, delivering a healthy double-digit volume and value growth that was broad-based across channels and key states,” chief executive and managing director Rakshit Hargave said.He said bakery products, businesses beyond biscuits and international operations also contributed to growth.However, total expenses increased 17.1% to Rs 4,690 crore from Rs 4,006 crore. Spending on raw materials, the largest expense, rose 22.3% to Rs 3,237 crore from Rs 2,647 crore.“We remain watchful of the inflationary pressures,” Hargave said. He also pointed to new products and cost efficiency as priorities for profitable growth.For the April-September period, consolidated net profit rose 12.3% to Rs 1,319 crore from Rs 1,175 crore. articles.title: Noel Tata to retire as Titan vice-chairman; Q2 profit more than doubles to Rs 2,393 cr
articles.summary: Noel Tata to retire as Titan vice-chairman on Nov 12; Q2 net profit jumps 114% to Rs 2,393 crore as income rises 13.8% and jewellery grows.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Noel Tata will retire as vice-chairman and director of Titan on Nov 12 under Tata group governance guidelines, the company said on Thursday. He has been associated with the jewellery and watches company since August 2003.The announcement came as Titan reported a 114% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 2,393 crore for the September quarter, from Rs 1,120 crore a year earlier.Total income increased 13.8% to Rs 21,430 crore from Rs 18,837 crore. Excluding bullion and digital gold sales and an accounting credit, the company put income growth at 25% to Rs 20,533 crore.The profit included a Rs 671 crore accounting gain linked to Titan’s acquisition of Damas. Titan reduced its estimated liability for buying the remaining 33% stake in the jeweller after geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East hurt Damas’ business. Excluding this credit, net profit rose 54% to Rs 1,722 crore.Profit also benefited from Rs 536 crore in gains arising from an increase in customs duty on gold. Excluding both gains, profit before tax grew 18% to Rs 1,793 crore.Jewellery income, excluding bullion and digital gold sales, rose 24% to Rs 17,495 crore. In India, Tanishq, Mia and Zoya together grew 20% to Rs 14,935 crore, while CaratLane’s income increased 31% to Rs 1,408 crore.Titan said jewellery growth was driven by higher average bills and demand for studded jewellery, which includes pieces set with diamonds or other stones. It added 42 jewellery stores, net of closures, in India during the quarter and opened a Tanishq outlet in Los Angeles.The watches business grew 27% to Rs 1,881 crore, while eyecare income increased 28% to Rs 281 crore. Managing director Ajoy Chawla said “consumer demand held up well for most of the period”, even as the festive calendar shifted to the December quarter.Titan’s board also approved raising up to Rs 2,500 crore through privately placed, unsecured non-convertible debentures, a form of debt.You use AI every day.
